name: equal-weight-10m-threshold-015-trade-to-band-edge
rationale: Literature-motivated cost-side hypothesis. Today every rebalance that clears allocation_threshold trades the full delta back to the target, so a target that oscillates around the band edge pays a full round trip each time. Optimal-rebalancing theory with proportional costs says to trade only back to the edge of the no-trade band, and NBIM (2018) finds that trading partially toward the target (inner bands) lowers turnover and costs. This keeps equal weights + 600s + threshold 0.15 (best diagnostic on record, 2026-10-31) and shrinks each order to |delta| - allocation_threshold. Caveat stated up front: at 50,000 JPY the smaller orders will fall under the 0.001 BTC lot floor more often, so 50k may trade even less and look degenerate; score on total_fees_jpy and 500k/5M diagnostics. Run the unmodified threshold-0.15 equal-weight code as an unregistered same-window reference.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), set TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT from 0.25 to 1.0 (REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT stays 1.0), exactly as experiment/equal-weight-rebalance-10m-threshold-015 (bc00fab) does. Nothing else in the function changes. Update both constants' doc comments and the compute_btc_target doc comment to record this probe. Update the compute_btc_target_* unit tests' expected values wherever the change legitimately alters them; rewrite (never delete) any test asserting reversion dominance. ADDITIONALLY: everywhere a rebalance order is sized from `delta = target_pct - current_alloc` after the `delta.abs() < allocation_threshold` check — TradingEngine::handle_indicator, TradingEngine::handle_rebalance, and Simulator::run in src/backtest/simulator.rs — pass `delta - delta.signum() * allocation_threshold` (trade to the band edge, not to the target) to allocation_delta_to_order instead of `delta`. Put that shrink in one small pure helper (e.g. `TradingEngine::band_edge_delta(delta, threshold) -> f64`) so live and backtest share it, with unit tests (positive, negative, exactly-at-threshold -> 0, threshold 0 -> unchanged). Do not change allocation_delta_to_order itself.
constraints: This hypothesis modifies the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. This change MUST be made only on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch -- never as a direct commit to dev/main.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) -- only its body.
MUST NOT change any individual sub-signal's own formula or the aggregation expression; exactly one numeric constant changes (TREND 0.25 -> 1.0).

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the compute_btc_target_* unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs -- update their expected values if the new weight legitimately changes them (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, so the reviewer gives it the scrutiny an allocation-formula change deserves.

MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/* or .github/workflows/*. This hypothesis DOES change rebalance order sizing on the live path (handle_indicator / handle_rebalance); that is intended, MUST go through the shared helper so the backtest exercises the same code, and MUST be flagged explicitly in any PR description as touching live order sizing.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's signature or any sub-signal formula; the only change inside compute_btc_target is TREND 0.25 -> 1.0.

paper_reference.title: No-trade band rebalancing rules: expected returns and transaction costs
paper_reference.key_claim: Wider no-trade bands, trading partially towards the strategic level (inner bands) and trading more slowly all lead to cost reductions and lower turnover; with proportional costs the optimal rebalance is to the band boundary.
paper_reference.pros: shirube already has a no-trade band (allocation_threshold) but always trades fully back to target; its cost is proportional (fee tier + slippage), exactly the case where band-edge rebalancing is optimal, and fee drag is the largest identified component of the deficit.
paper_reference.cons: The note concerns a fixed strategic equity share for a long-horizon fund, not a fast-moving signal target; its cost model is calibrated to large-cap equities with price impact; it shows that band drift captures time-varying returns only weakly; and at 50k the lot floor interacts with smaller orders.
